Given the exact 12 km / offshore-Gulf-of-Suez / SUMED match, and that SUMED Port, Ain Sokhna is independently reported (Daily News Egypt) to host FSRU marine-berth gas-import infrastructure feeding the national grid, the most likely read is that this is that offshore-to-terminal leg — but the two sources don't use identical terms for the same asset, so treat the FSRU-specific framing as an inference, not a directly stated fact. Got a solid, independently-sourced START this pass: the named 'SUMED Pipelines Terminal' facility itself (OSM-tagged industrial site + corroborating SUMED/port-authority sources), which anchors the marine/FSRU end of the line. STILL MISSING: no source names a specific tie-in facility for the onshore end -- articles only say gas is injected 'into the national grid' without naming a station. One same-day-reported GASCO facility, the 'National Gas Control Center (NATA)', came up in searches (Madbouly's Ain Sokhna visit continued to a NATA tour per an Egypt Oil & Gas piece) but the source explicitly does NOT state NATA is this pipeline's terminus or give NATA's location, so using it would be inference, not sourcing -- excluded per standing rule 2. (2) Downloaded and full-text-searched the EIB EIA for the historically related 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' (El-Tina East–El-Arish, 111 km, 32in, EIB project 20070088, PETROSAFE, Nov-2007) — https://www.eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia2_en.pdf. That original design already contained two internal 'LOOP' (duplicate-pipe) sections: LOOP#1 from the start point (km 00+00, agricultural area near El-Sheikh Gaber Canal, west-of-canal side) to km 32+00–33+00 near Romana villages; LOOP#2 from roughly km 84 to the km 111 end point near El-Midan Village (km 102–103) and on to El-Arish. This shows looping/duplicating this exact corridor is a recurring GASCO engineering pattern going back to 2007, but nothing ties the 2024/2025 'izdiwaj' projects to this specific 2007 EIA's loop segments — they could be new loops laid decades later at different km ranges, and no source states which. (3) Found (via Wayback Machine, since the live page now 404s/redirects) a 2020 soutalomma.com article confirming an EARLIER, separate 'Trans-Sinai gas line duplication' totaling 134 km built in two phases, explicitly to serve Sinai's own local consumption — establishing this is a recurring multi-decade capacity-expansion program on the corridor, not a one-off, but again with no named endpoints. (4) EcoConserv's public oil-and-gas project portfolio (ecoconserv.com/oil-gas/) lists several other GASCO EIA jobs (Raven pipeline, Giza North, Dahshour-Atfeeh, Nubaria-Metnama) but nothing Sinai-specific, consistent with the Nov-2025 consultation being too recent to be listed yet. No source anywhere names a specific facility, valve room, or km-point for the 15/15.5 km P8008 segment. Marking unresolved rather than guessing a corridor stretch. Recommended next steps for a future pass: (a) request the EEAA/Eco Conserve scoping document for the Nov-2025 consultation directly (it will very likely give exact km-point termini once public); (b) search the Ministry of Petroleum's and GASCO's own Facebook pages around 2024-06-08 for an inauguration post (these frequently name both tie-in stations); (c) if a fresh session restores WebSearch, target Petrojet/Enppi/Orascom Construction EPC contract-award announcements for 'khat izdiwaj 'abr Sinai'.

units.current_route_notes: CB: route guessed from endpoints — RESOLVED. Second pass identified 'Petreco Plant' as the Petreco Oil Centre, a Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum Co., the EGPC-Eni/IEOC joint operating company) oil-treatment and marine-terminal complex at Abu Rudeis, South Sinai Governorate -- the Sinai/east shore of the Gulf of Suez, opposite Ras Gharib. This also explains the pipeline's name: 'Trans Gulf Gas Pipeline' runs from Petrobel's Petreco Oil Centre on the Sinai side, across the Gulf of Suez, to Ras Bakr Transmission Station on the mainland/Red Sea Governorate side. Two independent sources: (1) Eni's 2016 corporate operations report for Egypt (Eni is Petrobel's foreign JV partner via IEOC) -- 'The Petreco Oil Center has a 260,000 barrels/day treatment capacity, and gathers some 85,000 barrels/day of oil from onshore and offshore fields -- Belayim Marine, Belayim Land, Abu Rudeis, Sinai and Ras Garra -- all operated by Petrobel'; (2) Egypt Oil & Gas news (2012) -- 'the main Petreco Oil Centre and marine terminal, [at Abu Rudeis]'. A third source (Egypt Oil & Gas, 'DCS System for Petreco Plant') corroborates it as a real, standing plant with its own control room, ruling out a one-off/typo name. Straight-line distance from the Abu Rudeis coordinate to the Ras Bakr endpoint is ~57-58 km -- clearly a distinct location, and consistent with the sheet's 75 km pipeline length once a Gulf-of-Suez water-crossing plus onshore routing overhead on both shores is factored in. Remaining minor uncertainty: the Eni text separately mentions Petreco (inland treatment) as 'connected to the Feiran tank farm and marine terminal' -- it's possible the actual gas offtake/loading point is the adjacent Feiran marine terminal rather than the inland Petreco treatment plant itself, but no source separately geocodes 'Feiran'; and no gazetteer/map names 'Petreco' directly, so the coordinate is a settlement-level proxy, not a surveyed plant footprint -- recommend RouteAccuracy stay moderate (not 'very high (within meters)') for this endpoint. abarrelfull.co.uk surfaced discussing this same facility in background search context and was excluded per standing rule, not used as a source. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet StartLocation 'Petreco Plant' is confirmed as an accurate, verbatim name (not a misspelling) -- it appears exactly as 'Petreco Plant' in the Egypt Oil & Gas table, and is corroborated as a standing facility name ('Petreco control room', 'Petreco Oil Centre') by two further independent sources found this pass. End coord basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Ra's Bakr' (point feature, N28 23'31" E33 3'42"), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt -- the nearest named public gazetteer entry to the transmission station named in the trade-press source below; GeoNames also separately lists a 'Ra's Bakr' oilfield ~14 km further NW (N28 29'0" E32 57'0"), confirming this as a real, long-standing place name in the Ras Gharib oil/gas cluster, not a typo.
